name: Pet Video Ideas
blurb: 45 pet and dog video ideas that keep animals comfortable, each with a hook and format
title: 45 Pet Video Ideas and Dog TikTok Ideas (With Hooks)
description: 45 pet video ideas for dogs, cats and small pets: daily life, training, voice-overs and stories, each with a 2-second hook and a format. Animal welfare first.
h1: 45 Pet Video Ideas, Each With a Hook and Format
answer: This list is for pet owners who want to film their animals in ways that are fun to watch and comfortable for the pet. Each idea says what to film, the hook for the first two seconds and the format, and none ask you to stress, scare or trick an animal.

items.t: Morning routine from the pet's side
items.d: Film at pet height from wake-up to breakfast. Hook: a nose appearing at the edge of the bed. Format: POV at floor level.
Show every favourite nap spot and score them. Hook: the strangest spot first. Format: voice-over.
One clip per corner of your usual route. Hook: the lead being picked up. Format: POV.

items.t: What my pet does when I get home
items.d: Set the phone by the door before you arrive. Hook: the key in the lock. Format: fixed camera.
Show how you prepare their food, following vet advice. Hook: the bowl tapping the floor. Format: hands only.

items.t: A tour of my pet's corner
items.d: Show bed, toys and water. Hook: the pet already lying in it. Format: voice-over.
Brushing or a bath done gently, stopping if the pet is unhappy. Hook: the before fluff. Format: before and after.
Indoor games on a wet afternoon. Hook: the pet staring at rain on the window. Format: vlog.

items.t: Pet reacts to a new toy
items.d: Unbox a safe toy and let them explore at their own pace. Hook: the box opening. Format: reaction.

items.t: Teaching a new trick with rewards
items.d: Show day one to the final result with positive reinforcement only. Hook: the finished trick first. Format: progress diary.
Make a treat puzzle from a box or towel. Hook: the pet's nose digging in. Format: DIY.
Let your dog lead a slow walk and narrate what they choose to sniff. Hook: a nose in a hedge. Format: voice-over.

items.t: Recall practice in a safe space
items.d: Show a step-by-step recall session in a fenced area. Hook: the pet sprinting toward the camera. Format: tutorial.

items.t: Cat play session with a wand toy
items.d: Show how you tire a cat out safely before bed. Hook: a pounce in slow motion. Format: close-up.
Hide treats around a room and let them search. Hook: the first find. Format: POV.
Practise a calm greeting routine. Hook: the doorbell sound. Format: tutorial.

items.t: A sensory garden for a small pet
items.d: Set up a safe space with pet-safe plants or textures. Hook: the first step in. Format: DIY.
A series where you teach a small, safe skill every week. Hook: the week number. Format: series.
Give your pet a voice that comments on your day. Hook: a pointed stare with the first line. Format: voice-over.
Narrate their judgement while they watch you cook, without feeding unsafe food. Hook: the stare at the pan. Format: voice-over.
Caption a calm walk like a live news broadcast. Hook: Breaking news from the park. Format: voice-over.
Read a dramatic diary of an ordinary day. Hook: Dear diary, the human left again. Format: voice-over.
Ask questions and caption imagined answers. Hook: a microphone held near the pet. Format: talking head.

items.t: My pet is the boss of the house
items.d: Show the pet sitting in your chair like an executive. Hook: the pet behind the laptop. Format: sketch.

items.t: A pet who thinks they are a ghost
items.d: Narrate their silent hallway patrols at night, gently spooky. Hook: glowing eyes in a dark corridor. Format: voice-over.
Caption their reaction to each guest, with guests' consent. Hook: the scorecard. Format: voice-over.
Subtitle each sound with an invented meaning. Hook: the first noise with a big subtitle. Format: captions.

items.t: A lost-dog poster with a twist
items.d: A lonely newcomer keeps finding the same lost-dog poster, calls the number and meets a neighbour with the dog. Hook: a poster taped to a pole. Format: story sketch.
A mock detective investigation into a missing sandwich. Hook: crumbs on the floor. Format: sketch.
Tell your adoption story with photos. Hook: the first photo together. Format: voice-over.

items.t: The day my pet came home
items.d: Recreate the arrival with the real pet and the old bed. Hook: the carrier door opening. Format: story.
Introduce a neighbour's pet they love, with the owner's agreement. Hook: two tails wagging. Format: vlog.

items.t: A night with a pet who cannot sleep
items.d: Play it as a gentle comedy with the pet waking you. Hook: a paw on your face at 3am. Format: sketch.

items.t: Life before and after a pet
items.d: Split screen of a tidy flat and the happy chaos now. Hook: the tidy side first. Format: split screen.
Play an over-prepared sitter with a long list. Hook: a ten-page instruction sheet. Format: sketch.
Celebrate a senior pet's simple joys. Hook: a grey muzzle in a sunbeam. Format: voice-over.

items.t: What I pack for a trip with my pet
items.d: Show the bag and why each item is there. Hook: the bag unzipping. Format: hands only.

items.t: Making the home safe for a new pet
items.d: Show cables tucked away and plants moved. Hook: a cable at floor level. Format: tutorial.
Share questions you were glad you asked a shelter. Hook: the first question in big text. Format: talking head.

items.t: How I keep my pet cool on hot days
items.d: Show shade, water and walk timing; follow vet guidance. Hook: a thermometer on the window. Format: tips.
Show your shift, with the shelter's permission. Hook: the volunteer badge. Format: vlog.

items.t: Rating pet products I have bought
items.d: Honest reviews of what your pet actually used. Hook: the product they ignored. Format: talking head.

items.t: A week of my pet's meals
items.d: Show portions and routine, not dietary advice. Hook: seven bowls lined up. Format: overhead.
Show what is in your kit and that you checked it with a vet. Hook: the kit opening. Format: hands only.
Photos from puppy or kitten days to now. Hook: the tiniest photo. Format: slideshow.

sections.h: How to pick and film a pet video
body: Start from what your pet already does naturally. The best pet videos are patient: you set up the camera, wait, and catch real moments rather than forcing a reaction.

ol: Pick one idea that fits your pet's personality and energy level.
Film at their eye level in good light, and keep the phone still on a surface or stand.
Record more than you need and stop as soon as your pet seems tired, stressed or uninterested.
Cut to 15 to 60 seconds, add captions or a voice-over, and keep natural sounds.
Post on a rhythm that never puts filming ahead of your pet's routine.

body.note: Animal welfare comes first: no scaring, costumes they dislike, unsafe food or treats, or challenges that stress the animal. Follow your vet's advice for care and diet.

ul: Open on the pet's face with the first line of a voice-over.
Show the finished trick first, then the training journey.
Start at floor level with a paw or nose entering the frame.
Use a dramatic caption over something ordinary: Breaking news.
Begin with a sound your pet reacts to, like the lead or a treat bag.
Show the strangest nap spot or position first.
Open on a before photo of a tiny puppy or kitten.

faq.q: How do I know my pet is okay with filming?
faq.a: Watch body language: flattened ears, tucked tails, hiding or lip licking mean stop. Keep sessions short and let the pet walk away whenever they want.

faq.q: Can I film The Lost Dog Poster with my own dog?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the dog stays safe and relaxed and is never actually lost. The script is original and free under CC BY 4.0; credit Script: cv.cm.

faq.q: What if my pet is not very active?
faq.a: Calm pets suit voice-over, diary and ambient ideas. A sleepy cat narrated as a stern manager can be funnier than any trick.
